result.question: Differentiate between tropical cyclones and extra-tropical (temperate) cyclones with respect to their origin, structure and behaviour. (Answer in 150 words)

sentences.text: Tropical and extra-tropical cyclones are both low-pressure systems with rotating winds, but they differ in origin, structure and behaviour.
Tropical cyclones originate over warm tropical oceans, whereas extra-tropical cyclones form along the polar front in the middle and high latitudes.
Extra-tropical cyclones have a clear frontal system with warm and cold fronts, which tropical cyclones lack.
Extra-tropical cyclones can originate over land or sea, while tropical cyclones form only over the seas and dissipate on reaching land.
Tropical cyclones affect a smaller area but have much higher wind speeds and are more destructive, with a calm central eye.
Tropical cyclones move from west to east, whereas extra-tropical cyclones move from east to west.
Because they need the Coriolis force, tropical cyclones do not form close to the equator.
They are called hurricanes in the Atlantic, typhoons in the western Pacific and willy-willies in north-western Australia.
As India's east coast is cyclone-prone, early warning, shelters and mangrove restoration remain key to reducing losses.
